alternative_explanations: Global oil and geopolitical shocks may have driven or contaminated longer-duration rates independently of the domestic decision.
A global bond-market sell-off may explain part of the market movement.
The NZD had already weakened before the decision, and no high-frequency reconstruction is available.
confounders: Pre-existing currency movement and source-reported rather than independently reconstructed event windows.
relationships.directionality_rationale: The reviewed policy-path information precedes the source-reported market response window; direction is analytical ordering, not causal proof.
falsification_conditions: High-frequency swap or FX data show the reported moves materially preceded the RBNZ release.
Later evidence shows the short-end move was primarily driven by a simultaneous global rates catalyst rather than the RBNZ path.
The market had priced an OCR path at or below the RBNZ projection immediately before the decision.
relationships.rationale: The expected 25 basis-point hike is not the surprise. The reviewed proposition concerns a more gradual forward path than market pricing and source-reported lower two-year swap and NZD pricing in the immediate/same-session window.

review_provenance.decision_basis: Accept the RBNZ association as a bounded historical relationship only; retain MEDIUM confidence, alternatives, confounders and falsifiers, and make no causal or current-active transmission claim.

relationships.revision_reason: First production revision: two separately reviewed World State component revisions were admitted in the same Step 11B transaction; shared lineage is not independent corroboration. Accepted as a historical association only; no causal promotion.

temporal_scope.notes: The RBNZ release is the event anchor. Market-response onset and end remain unknown within the source-reported immediate/same-session window; no exact temporal onset is manufactured.

relationships.title: RBNZ forward-path information and reported market repricing
